title: policy/commands.yaml
description: What commands Hermes may run, as argv-exact rules, and which built-in tools Pi workers get (spec §8.1). The matching semantics are in docs/policy.md and src/policy/commands.ts.

allow.description: Rule id -> an argv-exact rule. A command is allowed only if some rule matches its whole argv; everything else is denied (default-deny, fail-closed). Compiled into the hapi-cmd-allow hook (Plan 04), which must tokenize shell-aware and refuse shell operators before matching.

propertyNames.description: A rule id: a slug that starts with a letter, so every implementation keeps the rules in file order.

tools.description: Pi's built-in tools that worker nodes may use (Archon `allowed_tools`).

rule.description: An argv-exact rule. argv must start with exactly `command`. Every later token that starts with '-' is a flag and must be named in `flags`, spelled exactly; a flag with a `value` pattern takes the next token as its value. The other tokens are positionals: one per `args` pattern, in order, then up to `rest.max` more that match `rest.pattern`.

command.description: The exact leading tokens, e.g. [git, push, origin]. Anything before or between them, such as git's global options (`git -c ...`), means the rule doesn't match.

args.description: One pattern per required positional argument, in order.

rest.description: Optional positionals after `args`: at most `max` more, each matching `pattern`. Without `rest`, no extra positional is allowed.

flags.description: Flag -> {} for a flag without a value, or {value: pattern} for a flag whose value is the next token. Every other flag is denied, including --flag=value and bundled short flags (-abc).

propertyNames.description: A single dash and one letter or digit, or two dashes and a lowercase word.

pattern.description: A regular expression a whole token must match, written ^...$ and in the subset JavaScript (flags 'su') and Python (re.fullmatch, re.DOTALL) read the same way: no \d \w \s \b (or their capitals), \A \Z \z \p \k \g \c, backreferences, lookbehind, named groups or inline flags. Groups are (...), (?:...), (?=...) or (?!...); escapes are \n \r \t \f \v \xHH \uHHHH or a backslash before a non-alphanumeric character.
